Please review the following manuscript written by my collaborator.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b03/review-experiment-gp9m00eo/call-2b57cebe40ba499ca115cb7662ecf147/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo && command -v python3'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util
import shutil
for x in ['python3', 'pdftotext', 'pdftoppm', 'pdfinfo', 'gs']:
 print(x,shutil.which(x))
for x in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL']:
 print(x,importlib.util.find_spec(x))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1):
 t=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02}.txt').write_text(t)
 print(f'PAGE {i}: {len(t)} chars')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i} ===\\n'+p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout') for i,p in enumerate(r.pages,1)))
print(Path('tmp/pdfs/page-01.txt').read_text())
PY"

strengths: The virtual-correspondence formulation is an original, practically useful approach to difficult three-view pose problems. The mean-based variants turn four-point samples into inputs for established 5-point/6-point and P3P solvers, substantially simplifying implementation. This provides a meaningful contribution without requiring an exact algebraic solution.

The end-to-end results support the usefulness of the approach. In Table 1, 4p3v(M±0.15) improves Sacre Coeur median error from 3.04° for HC to 2.42°, and AUC@10° from 50.61 to 52.27. On KITTI, its partially calibrated counterpart achieves comparable accuracy to 6pt+P3P with lower reported RANSAC time, 0.07 versus 0.11 seconds.

The evaluation includes 10,000 real image triplets, controlled noise and outlier experiments, shift ablations, oracle comparisons, and conventional solvers using additional real correspondences. Figures 3 and 10 demonstrate benefits from sampling fewer correspondences under substantial outlier contamination.

The supplementary geometric lemma provides a rationale for mean-point correspondences. The manuscript also acknowledges approximation error and identifies circumstances where 5pt+P3P performs better. This transparency, together with the simple construction and documented network architecture, strengthens the contribution.
weaknesses: The claimed advantage under limited computational time is not fully established. Figures 3 and 8–10 compare RANSAC iterations, although an iteration has substantially different costs across methods: Table 1 reports 218.71 µs for M±δ versus 77.90 µs for 5pt+P3P, with learned variants substantially slower still. End-to-end timings are provided, but accuracy-versus-elapsed-time comparisons are needed to substantiate the specific high-outlier efficiency claim.

The evaluation does not measure all quantities involved in three-view reconstruction. The pose metric uses rotation and translation-direction errors for pairs 1–2 and 1–3, leaving relative baseline scale untested. No focal-length estimation errors are reported either. Consequently, Table 2 supports pose estimation in the tested KITTI setting but provides incomplete evidence for recovery of the full partially calibrated configuration; its stereo/adjacent-frame geometry also offers limited motion diversity.

The approximation's reliability remains insufficiently characterized. Lemma 1 bounds an image-space residual by triangle size; it does not establish a small pose error or a useful refinement basin. Figure 6 shows substantial errors even with noiseless observations. Analysis across baseline, depth variation, and perspective distortion would clarify failure conditions. These limitations matter for interpreting the method as an approximate hypothesis generator.

Equation (2) is a technical ambiguity in the learned method: its numerator is signed, without an absolute value or square, so the displayed objective is not a nonnegative Sampson loss. Minimizing it as written need not move predictions toward the epipolar line. This may be a correctable notation error, but the manuscript does not establish the actual training objective. The issue does not affect the mean-based solvers.

Experimental reproducibility is incomplete despite the useful supplementary details. RANSAC thresholds, termination criteria, and local refinement settings are not adequately specified. The normalization used when applying the calibrated network to unknown-focal-length inputs also needs clarification. Section 9.5 selects shifts using the reported evaluation scenes without documenting a separate tuning protocol, which warrants caution when interpreting small improvements.
